[Lab report organizer]
Based on the photo of my lab report — extract every test item and output strictly in this format (one line per item — never invent values — use ? for anything illegible):

Date: 2026-08-02
Hospital: Hospital name
Item, Result, Unit, Reference range, Flag
ESR, 15, mm/h, 0-20, Normal
CRP, 5.2, mg/L, 0-8, High
WBC, 6.1, 10^9/L, 3.5-9.5, Normal

Notes:
- Item is the name printed on the report (an English abbreviation may follow)
- Result is the value as printed (a number or Negative/Positive) with no unit
- Reference range copies the report verbatim (such as 2.9-8.2 or ≤5)
- Flag follows the report marking (High, High↑, Low, Normal)

[Imaging report organizer]
Based on the photo of my exam report (MRI/CT/X-ray) — extract the information and output strictly in this format:

Type: MRI (use the actual type reported — MRI / CT / X-ray)
Date: 2026-07-31
Hospital: Hospital name
Site: Sacroiliac joints
Findings: the full text of the imaging findings (may span several lines)
Conclusion: the full text of the diagnosis and impression (may span several lines)
Comparison: the change described against the previous scan (write None if absent)
This entry could not be parsed, so it was conservatively blocked. Please update the knowledge base seed data — bad data must not pass silently.
Do a reduced session today (half the range / shorter duration). %1$s
Do this only if your condition allows: gentle poses only, and keep the range pain-free. %1$s
Paused at your current stage (replaced by an L1 gentle item).
Not advised: fracture and stress risk rise with intensity.
Cervical spine involvement: this movement carries a high cervical risk
Pain worsened after exercise, but this fits muscle soreness (delayed onset). Watch it for 1–2 days; you may hold the duration steady next session (exc-010 progression rule).

Pain worsened after exercise and does not fit simple muscle soreness. By the 2-hour post-exercise pain rule, reduce the next session: cut the duration by 20% or drop the intensity one level (exc-010). If it worsens twice in a row, consider seeing a rehabilitation specialist.

Morning stiffness worsened — this may point to inflammatory activity rather than overexertion. Keep intensity low (L1) this week; if it keeps worsening, log your symptom trend and contact your doctor.
Good feedback. You can progress as planned: duration first (add 5–10 min every 1–2 weeks), then frequency, and intensity last.
Steady feedback. Keep the current amount. Progression order: duration → frequency → intensity (exc-010).
%1$s is already recorded (total %2$.1f). You can edit and resubmit to overwrite it.
Recorded at %1$s. Saving again will overwrite it.
Temperature today %1$s℃ ≥ the %2$s℃ threshold. Fever from infection must be assessed before the next biologic injection — see the emergency card.
Eye symptoms recorded (pain / redness / light sensitivity / blurred vision) — this may be uveitis; see an ophthalmologist as soon as possible.
Neurological symptoms recorded (numbness / weakness / changes in bowel or bladder control) — contact a doctor for assessment immediately.
The last 2 BASDAI self-assessments were both ≥%1$s (this one %2$s). Self-reported disease activity has stayed high; consider booking a rheumatology follow-up.

This flare is now on day %1$d. If self-care (rest / gentle activity / heat) brings no improvement within 7-10 days, contact the rheumatology team (frequent recurring flares may mean the treatment needs adjusting).
Knowledge entry \"%1$s\" is past its review date (%2$s) — the content may be out of date; when checking with your doctor, their advice takes precedence.
Recorded temperature %1$s℃ ≥ the %2$s℃ threshold. Fever from infection must be assessed before the next biologic injection — see the emergency card.

A live vaccine (%1$s) was recorded but the doctor\'s confirmation is still \"pending\" — live vaccines carry a serious infection risk for AS patients on biologics / DMARDs; confirm with your rheumatologist first (itx-010/012).
